explanation:
I found no Mathlib declaration that states this result. The theorem is the elementary Galois descent statement: an element of L ⊗[k] A is fixed by every k-automorphism of L acting on the left factor exactly when it has the form 1 ⊗ a. The library's proof is real work. It takes a basis of A, base-changes it to L, and applies InfiniteGalois.mem_range_algebraMap_iff_fixed to each coordinate. It also relies on Basis.map_baseChange_repr, which my grep did not find in Mathlib, so it is presumably the library's own. Searches made:
- Mathlib-wide greps for "TensorProduct.map … toLinearMap LinearMap.id", "map σ.toLinearMap", "rTensor … σ", "GaloisDescent", "galois descent" and "fixed … tensor"; none returned a match.
- fixedPoints, FixedPoints and IsInvariant in the TensorProduct, LinearAlgebra and FieldTheory directories; the only hits are unrelated files.
- Tensor-product files under FieldTheory (LinearDisjoint, PurelyInseparable, SeparablyGenerated); none has a descent statement.
- Mathlib's descent files, including RingTheory/Flat/FaithfullyFlat/Descent.lean, which only covers whether injectivity and surjectivity carry back along faithfully flat maps.
None of these contains a Galois-fixed-points-of-base-change result.
